bullets.title: Welcome to GNPS Program 7
bullets.text: Welcome to GNPS Program 7 - Caring for Children and Families. Paediatric nursing requires nurses to understand that infants, children and adolescents are not simply smaller adults. Their anatomy, physiology, communication, development, medication needs and responses to illness differ across age groups. This level is designed around the paediatric capabilities expected within national nursing educa…

bullets.title: Growth, Development and Family-Centred Care
bullets.text: Growth and development influence how children communicate, respond to illness, understand procedures and participate in care. Paediatric nurses must adapt assessment and intervention to developmental stage while recognising parents and carers as important partners.

bullets.title: Paediatric Assessment and Recognition of Deterioration
bullets.text: Paediatric assessment requires attention to age-specific vital signs, behaviour, breathing, circulation, hydration and neurological status. Children may compensate for illness before deteriorating suddenly, making early recognition essential.

bullets.title: Nursing Care for Common Childhood Conditions
bullets.text: Children commonly require nursing care for respiratory, cardiac, gastrointestinal, neurological and endocrine conditions. Safe care combines early recognition, evidence-based intervention and support for the child and family.

bullets.title: Medication Safety, Nutrition and Child Protection
bullets.text: Paediatric medication doses are commonly based on weight, and small errors can cause serious harm. Nutrition, hydration and safety are also central because children depend on adults for care and protection.
